1. iOS is a mobile operating system.
Subject: iOS, relation: instance of or subclass? Use "instance of" or "type"? The example used occupation, field of work. For OS, we can use "instance of" with object "mobile operating system". So relation: "instance of". object_type: "operating system". subject_type: "software". Might choose "software". Let's decide: subject_type "software". object_type "operating system". Include.

2. iOS developed by Apple Inc.
relation: "developer" or "developed by". Use "developer". Subject iOS, relation "developer", object Apple Inc. qualifiers none. subject_type software, object_type organization.

3. iOS designed for iPhone, iPad, iPod Touch (multiple). Should generate separate triplets for each: (iOS, platform, iPhone) maybe "operating system for". Use relation "operating system for". object_type "smartphone" for iPhone, "tablet computer" for iPad, "media player" for iPod Touch. Might generic "device". We'll use "operating system for". subject_type software, object_type device.

4. Updates for iOS are released through iTunes software.
Subject: iOS updates? The phrase "Updates for iOS are released through the iTunes software". So relation: "released through". Subject: iOS updates. But we may treat "iOS" as subject with relation "update distribution method". Could phrase: (iOS, update distribution, iTunes). Let's produce (iOS, update distribution method, iTunes). object_type software.

5. Since iOS 5, updates via over-the-air software updates.
Subject: iOS updates (or iOS) relation: "update distribution method" object: "over-the-air software updates". qualifiers: "point in time" "iOS 5". So we can have (iOS, update distribution method, over-the-air software updates) with qualifier point in time iOS 5. object_type: "software update method".

6. Announcement of iOS 5.0 on June 6, 2011.

7. With that announcement, a USB connection to iTunes was no longer needed to activate iOS devices.
We have fact: (USB connection to iTunes, not needed for, activation of iOS devices). That's negative claim. So subject: USB connection to iTunes, relation: "required for", object: "activation of iOS devices", qualifier polarity negative. subject_type: "hardware interface". object_type: "process". Could also be "activation of iOS devices". We'll include.

8. Data synchronization can happen automatically and wirelessly through Apple's iCloud service.
Subject: data synchronization (for iOS devices?) Probably "data synchronization" relation "method" "Apple's iCloud service". We'll have (data synchronization, performed through, iCloud service) qualifiers maybe "modality": "automatically and wirelessly". Not sure qualifiers: we could add qualifiers "modality" "automatic". But spec says modality qualifier for possible/planned etc. Not for automatic. Maybe we skip. We'll have (data synchronization, performed through, iCloud service). subject_type: "process". object_type: "service".

9. Major new iOS releases are announced yearly during WWDC.
Subject: iOS major new releases (or iOS releases). Relation: "announced at", object: Apple Worldwide Developers Conference. qualifier: "frequency" "yearly". But frequency not a qualifier type; we could use "recurrence" but not defined. Maybe just have (iOS major new release, announced at, Apple Worldwide Developers Conference). subject_type: "software version". object_type: "event". Add qualifier "recurrence" maybe not allowed. Could just not include.

10. Usually released in September of same year, coinciding with release of new iPhone models.
Subject: iOS major new releases, relation: "release month", object: September. qualifier: "point in time" maybe year unspecified. We'll include (iOS major new release, release month, September). subject_type software version, object_type month.

Also relationship with iPhone models: (iOS major new release, coincides with release of, new iPhone model). Could be generic.

11. Current stable release iOS 11.4 was released on May 29, 2018.
Subject: iOS 11.4, relation: "date of release", object: May 29, 2018. Also "stable release" maybe status. Could add (iOS 11.4, instance of, stable release). But maybe not needed. We'll include release date.
